To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Amino acid requirement data for poultry have been obtained with corn-soya diets containing 12% or 16% protein; (2) the amino acid requirement data obtained with the 16% protein basal diets were similar to those determined with 18 or 20% protein diets; (3) the requirement for lysine in the diet is not affected by the level of protein; (4) the requirements for tryptophan and isoleucine increase with the level

(1) a corn-soya diet containing 11.0% protein and 1.0% lysine is adequate for the maintenance of laying pullets and for their egg production and (2) a corn-so ya diet containing 11% protein, 1% lysine and 0.5% tryptophan is adequate for the development of laying pullets to 18 weeks of age and for their egg produc tion.

the addition of the following ingredients to a basal corn-soya diet containing 11.0% protein increased the performance of laying pullets: 0.25% DL-methionine, 0.10% L-lysine HCl, 0.05% L-tryptophan, and 0.05 to 0.10 % DL-methionyl hydroxy analog.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a practical corn-soya diet for laying pullets.
the amino acid requirements of poultry.
the amino acid requirements of laying pullets and the relationships between the dietary levels of amino acids, protein, energy and other nutrients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the requirement of laying pullets for the amino acids, isoleucine and lysine is 2.0 and 3.0 g./kg. of diet, respectively, with a tryptophan requirement of 0.3 g./kg.
the requirements for lysine, methionine and threonine in the corn-soya diet are 0.75, 0.25 and 0.25%, respectively.
the amino acid requirements of the laying hen are not yet fully defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the amino acid requirements for egg production can be met by diets which contain 12% of crude protein or less.
the requirement for lysine for laying hens is 1.0% of the diet and for isoleucin is 0.6% of the diet, and for tryptophan is 0.2% of the diet.
the requirement for the amino acid in question is 1.2% in the diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid requirements of laying hens are not the same as those of broilers.
we need to be careful in how we interpret amino acid requirement data.
it’s not the number of eggs you eat that matters most, but the type.
